title: Will Miguel Díaz-Canel leave office before 2026-11-01T15:00:00.000Z? Before November 1, 2026
rules: If Miguel Díaz-Canel leaves office before November 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary:
An announcement that the Miguel Díaz-Canel will leave the office within the next year is also encompassed by the Payout Criterion. If Miguel Díaz-Canel leaves solely because they have died, the associated market will resolve and the Exchange will determine the payouts to the holders of long and short positions based upon the last traded price (prior to the death). If a last traded price is not available or is not logically consistent, or if the Exchange determines at its sole discretion that the last traded prices prior to death do not represent a fair settlement value, the Outcome Review Committee will be responsible for making a binding determination of fair allocation.

Clarification (05/23/26): To clarify, Miguel Díaz-Canel currently holds two positions relevant to this market: First Secretary of the Communist Party of Cuba and President of Cuba. For purposes of this contract, departure from either position will satisfy the Payout Criterion.

blind.reasoning: As of Oct 22, 2026, Díaz-Canel holds both posts and is working normally (radio show, UN-vote diplomacy). He has publicly refused to resign despite heavy US pressure, sanctions and the indictment of Raúl Castro. With only about nine days left, YES would need a sudden shock such as US military action, an internal ouster, or a surprise announcement that he will leave within a year. Cuba's leadership rarely changes abruptly, so that's unlikely.
blind.falsifier: Before Nov 1, 2026, the Cuban government announces that Díaz-Canel is resigning or being replaced as President or First Secretary (or will be within a year), or a US operation removes him from power.

final.reasoning: The 11% midpoint likely reflects general fear of a US move or a sudden reshuffle rather than any concrete sign. With nine days left and Díaz-Canel visibly governing and refusing to resign, I nudge my estimate up only slightly to 4%, still well below the market.
